READING

**Net annual saving – dead mileage first**

Culverstone is 3 miles further each way from the 44 stand. Each of the 22 network vehicles makes at least one outward and one return dead-mileage leg per operating day.

22 vehicles × 313 days × 6 miles × £0.63 = **£26,029/year** in extra running cost.

Rent saving (ARDENSHAW minus KESTERWICK): £214,000 − £118,000 = £96,000/year.
Net annual saving at Culverstone after dead mileage: £96,000 − £26,029 = **£69,971/year**.
Over the ten-year term that is £699,710 before one-time items.

---

**One-time costs under KESTERWICK**

The planning application was validated on 14 August 2026. At 34-week median, consent arrives around 10 April 2027 – well after the 5 December 2026 free-option window. The £40,000 deposit is effectively certain.

| Item | £ |
|---|---|
| Faskally deposit (December 2026) | 40,000 |
| Build-out | 480,000 |
| Sub-total committed | **520,000** |

---

**Planning scenarios and Nethercote exposure**

*Validation date: 14 August 2026. Works: 22 weeks from consent.*

| Scenario | Consent | Works done | Hallowbrand ends | Nethercote needed? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Target (13 wk) | 13 Nov 2026 | 30 Apr 2027 | 30 Nov 2027 | No |
| Median (34 wk) | 10 Apr 2027 | 18 Sept 2027 | 30 Nov 2027 | No |
| Slowest (61 wk) | 15 Oct 2027 | 15 Mar 2028 | 30 Nov 2027 | Dec 2027 – Mar 2028 |

In the slowest case Nethercote runs roughly four months at £18,500/month ≈ **£74,000**, plus unquantified workshop-outsourcing premium. Even adding that, the ten-year net position is:

- **Median / no Nethercote:** £699,710 − £520,000 = £179,710 saved
- **Slowest / Nethercote:** £699,710 − £594,000 = £105,710 saved

KESTERWICK is positive in every scenario that ends with consent.

---

**Cash position**

Available: £640,000 cash + £200,000 undrawn = **£840,000**.

Deposit in December 2026: −£40,000 → £800,000 remaining.
Build-out in mid-2027: −£480,000 → **£320,000 remaining before drawing the facility**.

The business continues to generate cash between now and the build, and the build cost itself can be staged across 22 weeks. The facility stays untouched as a reserve through the construction phase. Tight, but adequate.

---

**The September 2027 bid – the number that matters most**

The 44/44A contract bid lands on 14 September 2027. Depot cost enters as a fixed line.

Under ARDENSHAW that line is £214,000. Under KESTERWICK (median scenario, works done 18 September 2027) the Culverstone lease is signed and consent is in hand by bid date; the line is £118,000. The difference is £96,000/year – and if the contract runs five years that is nearly half a million pounds of headroom in a tendered submission. Underbidding a competitor by £96,000/year in depot cost alone can be the margin that retains the network.

Even in the slow scenario, where consent arrives in October 2027, consent plus signed Culverstone lease is sufficient evidence for the procurer; the operator is bidding a committed, documented cost, not a wish.

Under ARDENSHAW the depot cost is certain but it is a permanently elevated number carried into every future bid.

---

**The planning-refusal tail risk**

This is the only scenario that is genuinely harmful. If Verrancombe refuses consent after 19 December 2026 (when the Hallowbrand offer has lapsed), Trentmoor holds a £40,000 sunk cost, no long-term site, and a Hallowbrand landlord who now knows they are exposed. Nethercote at £222,000/year with no workshop is an operational and financial emergency.

That risk must be acknowledged. However:
- The application is already validated on a site presumably chosen for suitability;
- Refusal would be unusual for an established operator seeking a depot of this kind;
- The Culverstone option remains live until June 2028 (post-deposit), giving time to appeal or submit a revised application;
- Nethercote is month-to-month and provides an emergency bridge, expensive as it is.

The refusal scenario is real but is a tail event, not the central case, and the Culverstone option window extends well beyond any likely appeal resolution.

---

**Long-term position**

ARDENSHAW commits Trentmoor to Hallowbrand tenancy at £214,000/year until 2037 – at which point they re-enter a renewal from the same exposed position they would be in today, but at a higher base. KESTERWICK amortises £520,000 of capital across ten years of £69,971/year net saving, recovers it in roughly 7.5 years, and exits 2037 with a fully fitted, ten-year-old depot whose improvements are long paid for.

---

**Summary**

KESTERWICK delivers a ten-year net saving of £106,000–£180,000 depending on how planning runs. More importantly, it puts a depot cost of £118,000 rather than £214,000 into the September 2027 bid – a £96,000/year structural competitive advantage in a tendered market where that line is fixed and visible. The cash position supports execution. The Nethercote fall-back is available and understood. ARDENSHAW's certainty is real, but its price is overpaying by £96,000/year for ten years and entering every future contract round from a weaker cost base.

---

CALL
KESTERWICK

GROUNDS
The £96,000-per-year depot cost advantage that Culverstone puts into the September 2027 contract bid – and every subsequent tender – outweighs the execution risk, given that the cash position supports the build, Nethercote provides a viable bridge in the worst planning scenario, and the ten-year net saving is positive under every outcome that stops short of planning refusal.
